flags.statement: Truth is ONE SPECIES OF GOOD, and not, as is usually supposed…
flags.reason: Quote begins "truth is ONE SPECIES OF GOOD" and the statement reads fine, but "Truth" is not tied to any named speaker. This is a general claim and reads alone, so no fault. (Not flagged; ignore.)

flags.h1: 7 The True Is the Good in the Way of Belief
flags.file: 7 The True Is the Good in the Way of Belief.md
flags.statement: But in this world, certain ideas are not only agreeable…
flags.reason: The source reads "just as certain foods are not only agreeable to our taste, but good for our teeth, our stomach and our tissues; so certain ideas are…". The cut drops the food analogy and the "so", which linked the claim to its argument. The joined statement is fine on its own, but the quotes splice "But in this world" onto the second half of a "just as… so…" sentence.

flags.reason: "no" refers to the previous question ("can we keep… permanently apart?"), which is in the note, so that part resolves. The author name span "William James" is cut-wise questionable (see below).

flags.h1: 7 The True Is the Good in the Way of Belief
flags.file: 7 The True Is the Good in the Way of Belief.md
flags.statement: My belief in the Absolute, based on the good it does me, must run the gauntlet of all my other beliefs.
flags.reason: "the Absolute" is not introduced anywhere earlier in the note. The same applies to "Grant that it may be true in giving me a moral holiday." ("it", "moral holiday"), "It happens to be associated…", "I just TAKE my moral holidays…", "If I could restrict my notion of the Absolute to its bare holiday-giving value…", and "My disbelief in the Absolute…". Each depends on the Absolute and the "moral holiday" discussion from the previous section.
